name: Skate Punk
about: Skate punk is the fast, melodic strain of hardcore that grew up alongside skateboarding in Southern California and Arizona in the early 1980s, when JFA, Agent Orange and Suicidal Tendencies soundtracked the empty pools and Thrasher magazine tapes. Bad Religion's Suffer rebuilt it in 1988 around harmonized vocals and Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph label, and Fat Mike's Fat Wreck Chords and NOFX made it the dominant 1990s punk sound: double-time drums, palm-muted guitar runs, singable choruses and a joke never far away. Pennywise, Lagwagon, Strung Out and No Use for a Name filled the Warped Tour and the Tony Hawk video games; Propagandhi and Millencolin carried it to Canada and Sweden. It is technical for punk, apolitical mostly, and still thriving in the same clubs.

artists.name: JFA
artists.why: Phoenix skaters who named the genre's spirit

artists.name: Agent Orange
artists.why: surf guitar meets Orange County hardcore

artists.name: NOFX
artists.why: Fat Mike's label and the 1990s template

artists.name: Pennywise
artists.why: Hermosa Beach anthems for the pit

artists.name: Lagwagon
artists.why: Joey Cape's melodic, drum-driven Goleta band

artists.name: No Use for a Name
artists.why: Tony Sly's bittersweet Fat Wreck mainstays

artists.name: Rise Against
artists.why: took melodic hardcore to the arenas

albums.title: Living in Darkness
albums.why: Mike Palm's surf-guitar instrumentals and Bloodstains inside a hardcore debut invented the skate-punk sound before there was a scene to use it.

albums.title: Valley of the Yakes
albums.why: Jodie Foster's Army's first full album mixed surf covers and sixty-second thrashers, the Phoenix skate scene's founding document.

albums.title: Suicidal Tendencies
albums.why: Institutionalized and Mike Muir's Venice gang persona brought skate culture and the first hints of thrash crossover into hardcore's biggest early seller.

albums.title: Lullabies Help the Brain Grow
albums.why: Austin's funk-playing skate punks, led by the late Randy Biscuit Turner, made their most varied record and told everyone to go start a band.

albums.title: Rock 'n' Roll Nightmare
albums.why: Rich Kids on LSD played faster and more precisely than anyone in the Nardcore scene, and Bomer's drumming here was the model for the next decade.

albums.title: Suffer
albums.why: Greg Graffin's vocabulary and the three-part harmonies on fifteen fast songs revived Southern California punk and set up the 1990s melodic boom.

albums.title: No Control
albums.why: Faster and tighter than Suffer, with I Want to Conquer the World and the title track, it is the record most of Fat Wreck Chords learned to play from.

albums.title: Pennywise
albums.why: Jim Lindberg's Hermosa Beach quartet's debut set surf-punk guitar to positive hardcore shouts, and Bro Hymn became the genre's communal anthem.

albums.title: White Trash, Two Heebs and a Bean
albums.why: The first NOFX record with El Hefe, where the humor, ska breaks and speed came together, with Bob and Stickin' in My Eye as proof.

albums.title: Don't Turn Away
albums.why: Trever Keith's Victorville band paired Disconnected's chorus with earnest, gruff melody, the record that got skate punk on KROQ.

albums.title: Punk in Drublic
albums.why: Linoleum, Don't Call Me White and Fat Mike's wit at full tempo made the genre's definitive record, a million seller without a video or a major label.

albums.title: Hoss
albums.why: Joey Cape's melodies and Derrick Plourde's drumming on Violins and Razor Burn made the Goleta band's third album the Fat Wreck catalog's fan favorite.

albums.title: Hero of Our Time
albums.why: Sweden's Satanic Surfers, with a singing drummer, played the Fat Wreck style faster than most Californians on their Burning Heart debut.

albums.title: For God and Country
albums.why: Russ Rankin's political Santa Cruz hardcore at melodic speed gave Fat Wreck Chords its most serious band and this, its most urgent early record.

albums.title: Less Talk, More Rock
albums.why: Chris Hannah's Winnipeg band's second album is anarchist, vegan and funny, with Apparently I'm a P.C. Fascist as the manifesto and the hook.

albums.title: Suburban Teenage Wasteland Blues
albums.why: Jason Cruz's melodies over Rob Ramos's metal-schooled guitar made the Simi Valley band's second album the genre's most technically accomplished.

albums.title: Making Friends
albums.why: Tony Sly's bittersweet songwriting on On the Outside and Invincible gave the San Jose band's fourth album more heart than its Fat Wreck peers.

albums.title: Let's Talk About Feelings
albums.why: After Plourde's departure, the band's tightest and most melodic record, with May 16 the song every skate-punk fan can sing.

albums.title: Pennybridge Pioneers
albums.why: Recorded in California with Brett Gurewitz, the Örebro band's fourth album added No Cigar and Fox to the Tony Hawk generation's canon.

albums.title: Revolutions per Minute
albums.why: Tim McIlrath's Chicago band's second album, before the major label, is melodic hardcore at skate-punk velocity with real political anger.

albums.title: Ruiner
albums.why: The New Bedford band's dizzying guitar harmonies and Nuno Pereira's rasp made the most technically demanding skate punk record of the 2000s.

albums.title: Supporting Caste
albums.why: The band's thrash-metal turn reached full force on Night Letters and Dear Coach's Corner, political skate punk at its most muscular.

albums.title: Partycrasher
albums.why: Six years after Career Suicide, the band returned with the same tangled guitar lines and a sharper production, for the faithful mostly.

albums.title: Go to Prison
albums.why: The New Orleans band compressed hardcore fury and sudden pop choruses into a twenty-minute debut that Fat Wreck Chords picked up almost immediately.
